title: Art
coreMove: Ask how difficulty, waste, and external validation make artistic value legible as a costly signal.
sourcePressure: The source reads art through costly signaling and the handicap principle, where impracticality and extrinsic features help signal value.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The writer turns art into personal expression or taste debate and misses costly signaling.

sourceAnchors.name: costly signaling
sourceAnchors.detail: The source says art can be understood through costly signaling.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The useless effort can be exactly what makes the signal credible.

sourceAnchors.name: the handicap principle
sourceAnchors.detail: The source names the handicap principle as part of the art account.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A hard-to-fake burden can make value easier to believe.

sourceAnchors.name: impracticality and extrinsic features signaling value
sourceAnchors.detail: The source says impracticality and extrinsic features help explain how art signals value.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The frame, venue, and waste of effort can speak before the image does.

exampleSpecs.audience: a programmer choosing between competent and difficult films
exampleSpecs.stakes: difficulty may signal seriousness but can crowd out audience clarity
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Andrew places the one-take film beside audience notes and asks whether its impracticality proves discipline or merely flatters the jury.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A stack of screeners leans against the projector case.

exampleSpecs.audience: a curator explaining why installation labor matters
exampleSpecs.stakes: viewers may read effort before meaning
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Manon leaves the rigging photos visible near the wall label so the hanging stones signal cost without needing a lecture.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Steel cable hums faintly above the gallery floor.

exampleSpecs.audience: a potter deciding whether to display failed test pieces
exampleSpecs.stakes: visible waste can make mastery legible
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "Show the warped ones," Jonas says, and Marta sees customers understand the price only after touching the failed glaze tiles.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Show the warped ones," Jonas says while Marta unwraps the perfect bowl.

exampleSpecs.audience: a student deciding how much process to reveal
exampleSpecs.stakes: process can signal costly skill rather than hide weak concept
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You have Diego pin the discarded models beside the final one, making the jury see the search cost before debating taste.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You see balsa scraps under the final white model.

exampleSpecs.audience: a conductor assessing a score full of impossible passages
exampleSpecs.stakes: technical burden may signal value or vanity
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Does the passage sound impossible because it earns the moment or because it asks the orchestra to applaud the composer?
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Does the impossible bar earn its difficulty after the rehearsal stops?

exampleSpecs.audience: an organizer making extrinsic value visible without faking prestige
exampleSpecs.stakes: the site, process, and community signatures alter how the work is read
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It took Hiroshi one denied permit to realize the council never saw the scaffolding plan, school sketches, and signed maintenance pledge that made the mural costly.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Hiroshi one denied permit to understand what the council had not seen.

skillTargets: apply costly signaling to artistic value
distinguish impractical value signals from empty difficulty
explain the role of extrinsic features without reducing art to status only

tryThisNowSpec: Choose one artwork or creative object near you. List what is costly or impractical about it, then ask what that cost makes credible.
